data.title: Notoginsenoside R1 Alleviates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury via MAPK/mTOR-Mediated Autophagy.
data.authors: Li S, Liu Z, Pan G, Li Y, Lv K
data.journal: The American Journal of Chinese Medicine

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Notoginsenoside R1 alleviates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury by activating protective autophagy through MAPK/mTOR pathway modulation, reducing hepatocyte death and oxidative damage.
data.abstract_excerpt: Notoginsenoside R1 (NGR1), a bioactive saponin from Panax notoginseng, was investigated in acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury (AILI). NGR1 treatment activated autophagy via modulation of the MAPK/mTOR pathway, reducing hepatocyte apoptosis and oxidative stress, and attenuating liver injury in mouse models and hepatocyte cultures.

extracted_findings.effect: NGR1 suppresses mTOR to activate autophagy, reducing APAP-induced hepatocyte apoptosis and liver injury
